text: Your army has spotted something in the surrounding area that may have been of interest to you, but you were marching too fast to have time to see what it was. Switch to default stance before returning to the location to take a closer look.
We passed a smithy without stopping. Perhaps a lord should come back to see what it holds.

The Master Blacksmith Is Ready To Receive You
The master blacksmith sends word that the forge is ready again. Send a lord to the smithy to choose from his new work.

We have occupied this abandoned smithy. It has ample room, tools and workshops to craft work of excellent quality. A new master smith of our kingdom now leads its artisans, and the detachment we assigned to him will defend it. May it produce the best for the kingdom.

We have visited a smithy belonging to a neighboring kingdom. The master blacksmith speaks to us from the walls of the building and tells us news of his kingdom, but he never lets us in. Only through war or the destruction of its owning faction can we take control of the smithy and appoint a blacksmith of our own. Maybe we should take it?

We have given the master blacksmith a large sum to improve the smithy and strengthen the garrison that protects it. The artisans rejoice: new tools and a larger workshop let them keep more craftsmen and forge equipment of even better quality. The forge will be ready for visits sooner, and they promise to send tribute more often. All for the good of the kingdom!

We sent the master blacksmith and the garrison an urgent order to retreat, and they obeyed. The enemy has taken the smithy and its forge has lost a level, but our people live to fight another day. We will get the smithy back in time.

The enemy army has been routed and their master blacksmith slain along with most of his disciples. We occupy the well-equipped smithy with our own master blacksmith and assign a detachment of soldiers to protect him and his disciples. They will send us tribute regularly, and our lords can visit the forge to choose from its new work. Everything for the good of the kingdom!
Our army has been driven back from the smithy. Its defenders held the forge this time, but a smithy guarded so fiercely is worth taking. We should return with a stronger force.
Hammers and blades alike lie red on the field. The enemy broke and fled, and the smithy still stands over its lands like a lord's keep. The forge will work another day.

We lost control of the smithy. We saved the master blacksmith and some of his disciples, but the forge has lost a level, and we lose both its tribute and our visits to it. We should recapture it as soon as we can.
An enemy army has surrounded our smithy. At the start of our turn we must decide whether to defend it or give it up.
We could not raise a garrison in time. The raiders looted the forge before leaving, and it has lost a level of craft.
